title: THE LORD ALONE IS MY GOD

memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "Laban also said to Jacob, 'Here is this heap, and here is this pillar I have set up between you and me. This heap is a witness, and this pillar is a witness, that I will not go past this heap to your side to harm you and that you will not go past this heap and pillar to my side to harm me. May the God of Abraham and the God of Nahor, the God of their father, judge between us.' So Jacob took an oath in the name of the Fear of his father Isaac. He offered a sacrifice there in the hill country and invited his relatives to a meal. After they had eaten, they spent the night there. Early the next morning Laban kissed his grandchildren and his daughters and blessed them. Then he left and returned home." - Gen 31:51-55 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
The two men agree on a boundary: neither will cross this heap to harm the other. Then a small but telling detail appears. Laban swears by "the God of Abraham and the God of Nahor" — mixing the true God together with the gods of his own family line. But Jacob will not do that. He takes his oath only "in the name of the Fear of his father Isaac" — that is, the one true God alone. Jacob refuses to blur the living God together with idols.

This is a sign of Jacob's growth. After twenty years of shaping and testing, he is clearer than ever about who his God is. He will not lump the Lord in with other so-called gods. His loyalty is settling on the one true God alone.

Then comes a gentle end to a hard story. Jacob offers a sacrifice, shares a meal with everyone, and in the morning Laban kisses his grandchildren, blesses his daughters, and goes home in peace. A conflict that could have ended in bloodshed ends instead in a shared meal and a blessing.

God had watched over the whole tense encounter and brought Jacob through safely. As we follow the Lord, may we too grow clearer in our devotion to Him alone, and trust Him to carry us peacefully through our hardest confrontations.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Am I clear, like Jacob, that the Lord alone is my God — not one option among many?
2. Where do I need to stop blurring God together with other loyalties?
3. Can I trust God to carry me peacefully through a hard confrontation?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Lord, You alone are my God; keep me from blurring You together with any other loyalty. Thank You for carrying me through hard encounters. Settle my devotion on You alone. Amen.
